docs.text: Run each solution from the repository root with the practice site running. Each one runs pytest on a test file in the lesson folder, as the worked example does.

docs.title: Exercise 1: a relative sign-in test
docs.text:
Write a test that signs in as ada and asserts the welcome message. Use goto("login.html"), not a full URL, and pass the site's address with --base-url. Run it and check it passes.

Solution

The test, exercises/test_sign_in.py:

"""Lesson 09, exercise 1: a sign-in test with a relative URL, run by ``solution_1_sign_in_test.py``.

    pytest examples/course/09-pytest-plugin/exercises/test_sign_in.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8765/

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from steero.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_sign_in_shows_the_welcome_message(steero_page: Page) -> None:
    steero_page.goto("login.html")  # resolved against --base-url
    steero_page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
    steero_page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
    steero_page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
    expect(steero_page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")

The script that runs it:

"""Lesson 09, exercise 1: run a sign-in test whose ``goto("login.html")`` relies on ``--base-url``.

The test is ``exercises/test_sign_in.py``; this script runs it and checks that it passed.

    python examples/course/09-pytest-plugin/solution_1_sign_in_test.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from pytest_run import run_pytest

# course: timeout=180

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "09-pytest-plugin" / "exercise-1"


def main() -> None:
    args = [str(HERE / "exercises" / "test_sign_in.py"), "-v",
            "--steero-browser", BROWSER, "--steero-base-url", BASE_URL]
    if not HEADLESS:
        args.append("--steero-headed")
    outcome = run_pytest(*args, out=OUT)
    assert outcome.exit_code == 0 and outcome.passed == 1, outcome
    print("The sign-in test passed with a relative URL.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Without --base-url, goto("login.html") has nothing to resolve against and the navigation fails. That is the point: the address lives in one place, the command line.

docs.title: Exercise 2: both browsers, and their test ids
docs.text:
Ask pytest for the worked example's tests in Chrome and Firefox, and read the ids it gives them. How many tests are there, and how does each id name its browser?

Hint: --collect-only -q lists the tests without running them.

Solution 
"""Lesson 09, exercise 2: ask for two browsers and read the test ids pytest gives each test.

``--collect-only`` lists the tests without running them, so no browser is started. Drop it
(and keep both ``--steero-browser`` options) to run the suite in Chrome and then Firefox.

    python examples/course/09-pytest-plugin/solution_2_test_ids.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from pytest_run import run_pytest

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "09-pytest-plugin" / "exercise-2"


def main() -> None:
    outcome = run_pytest(str(HERE / "tests"), "--collect-only", "-q",
                         "--steero-browser", "chrome", "--steero-browser", "firefox", out=OUT)
    assert outcome.exit_code == 0, outcome
    ids = [line.split("::", 1)[1] for line in outcome.output.splitlines() if "::" in line]
    print(f"{len(ids)} test ids:")
    for test_id in ids:
        print("   ", test_id)
    # Each test appears once per browser, with the browser in square brackets.
    assert "test_products_table_loads[chrome]" in ids and "test_products_table_loads[firefox]" in ids, ids
    assert len(ids) == 6, ids


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

6 test ids:
    test_home_page_lists_the_course_pages[chrome]
    test_home_page_lists_the_course_pages[firefox]
    test_products_table_loads[chrome]
    test_products_table_loads[firefox]
    test_deliberately_wrong_title[chrome]
    test_deliberately_wrong_title[firefox]

Three tests times two browsers. Remove --collect-only to run them all; all the Chrome runs share one Chrome, and all the Firefox runs share one Firefox.

docs.title: Exercise 3: read the evidence
docs.text:
Run only the failing test (-k wrong_title), then open its screenshot.png and diagnostics.json. What URL was the page on, and what did the console say?

Solution 
"""Lesson 09, exercise 3: make a test fail, then read the artifacts the plugin saved for it.

Runs only the deliberately failing test (``-k wrong_title``), then prints where its screenshot is
and what ``diagnostics.json`` recorded: the page URL and the console message the test logged.

    python examples/course/09-pytest-plugin/solution_3_failure_artifacts.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from pytest_run import run_pytest

# course: timeout=180

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "09-pytest-plugin" / "exercise-3"


def main() -> None:
    shutil.rmtree(OUT, ignore_errors=True)
    args = [str(HERE / "tests"), "-k", "wrong_title", "--tb=line",
            "--steero-browser", BROWSER, "--steero-base-url", BASE_URL, "--steero-artifacts", str(OUT / "artifacts")]
    if not HEADLESS:
        args.append("--steero-headed")
    outcome = run_pytest(*args, out=OUT)
    assert outcome.failures == 1, outcome

    (folder,) = (OUT / "artifacts").iterdir()
    screenshot = folder / "screenshot.png"
    assert screenshot.read_bytes()[:4] == b"\x89PNG"
    print("Open this screenshot:", screenshot)

    diagnostics = json.loads((folder / "diagnostics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print("Page URL when it failed:", diagnostics["url"])
    print("Console:", diagnostics["console"])
    assert diagnostics["url"].endswith("login.html")
    assert "[log] checking the title" in diagnostics["console"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Open this screenshot: ...\exercise-3\artifacts\tests_test_shop.py_test_deliberately_wrong_title_chrome\screenshot.png
Page URL when it failed: http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html
Console: ['[log] checking the title']

The test logged that console line itself, to show where console output ends up. In a real suite this is where you find the app's own errors.

docs.title: Exercise 4: start signed in
docs.text:
Add a conftest.py with a signed_in_page fixture that signs in on steero_page and returns it. Write two tests that use it: one checks the title changed to "Welcome - steero practice site", the other that localStorage remembers the user name. While you are there, override steero_launch_options to use a 1024 by 768 window.

Solution

exercises/conftest.py:

"""Lesson 09, exercise 4: fixtures shared by the tests in this folder.

pytest loads a ``conftest.py`` automatically for every test beside it or below it, so the
fixtures here need no import.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from typing import Any

import pytest

from steero.sync_api import Page, expect


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def steero_launch_options(steero_launch_options: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The plugin's launch options (headless or headed, backend), plus a smaller window."""
    return {**steero_launch_options, "window_size": (1024, 768)}


@pytest.fixture
def signed_in_page(steero_page: Page) -> Page:
    """A page that has already signed in as ada; each test still gets its own fresh context."""
    steero_page.goto("login.html")
    steero_page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
    steero_page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
    steero_page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
    expect(steero_page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
    return steero_page

exercises/test_signed_in.py:

"""Lesson 09, exercise 4: tests that start signed in, using ``signed_in_page`` from ``conftest.py``.

    pytest examples/course/09-pytest-plugin/exercises/test_signed_in.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8765/

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from steero.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_title_changes_after_sign_in(signed_in_page: Page) -> None:
    expect(signed_in_page).to_have_title("Welcome - steero practice site")


def test_user_name_is_remembered(signed_in_page: Page) -> None:
    assert signed_in_page.evaluate("localStorage.getItem('user')") == "ada"

And the script that runs them:

"""Lesson 09, exercise 4: tests that start signed in, through a fixture in ``conftest.py``.

Runs ``exercises/test_signed_in.py``; its ``signed_in_page`` fixture comes from
``exercises/conftest.py``, which also overrides ``steero_launch_options``.

    python examples/course/09-pytest-plugin/solution_4_signed_in_fixture.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from pytest_run import run_pytest

# course: timeout=180

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "09-pytest-plugin" / "exercise-4"


def main() -> None:
    args = [str(HERE / "exercises" / "test_signed_in.py"), "-v",
            "--steero-browser", BROWSER, "--steero-base-url", BASE_URL]
    if not HEADLESS:
        args.append("--steero-headed")
    outcome = run_pytest(*args, out=OUT)
    assert outcome.exit_code == 0 and outcome.passed == 2, outcome
    print("Both tests started on a signed-in page.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The fixture ends with an expect, so a test never starts on a page that is still signing in. Each test still gets its own context: the second test is signed in because the fixture ran again, not because the first test's state leaked into it.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Common mistakes

  • fixture 'page' not found. steero's fixture is steero_page. Use that name, or add the page alias to conftest.py.
  • unrecognized arguments: --browser (or --base-url), or the option seems ignored. pytest-playwright or pytest-base-url is installed and owns the plain name. Use the --steero- spelling: --steero-browser, --steero-base-url.
  • ProtocolError: browsingContext.navigate: invalid argument: Invalid URL: login.html. A relative goto() with no base URL to resolve against. Pass --base-url, or put it in addopts in pytest.ini.
  • ScopeMismatch when overriding steero_launch_options. The override must be scope="session", like the original, because the session-wide browser depends on it.
  • A test passes alone and fails in the full run. Something is shared outside the browser, or a test created its own context with steero_browser.new_context() and never closed it. Contexts from steero_context are closed for you; your own are not.
  • Looking for artifacts in the wrong folder. Failure artifacts go to steero-artifacts/; --screenshot, --video and --tracing files go to --output (test-results/). Both are relative to the folder you ran pytest from.
  • timeout=5000 in a test. Timeouts are seconds here too, also in --steero-timeout.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• Ask for steero_page in a test and the plugin launches, isolates and cleans up for you: one browser per session, a fresh context per test.
  • --browser chrome --browser firefox runs every test in each browser; the browser is part of the test id.
  • --base-url keeps addresses out of tests; --screenshot, --video and --tracing keep evidence per test in --output.
  • A failing test always leaves screenshot.png, page.html and diagnostics.json in steero-artifacts/<test id>/.
  • Put shared fixtures and option overrides in conftest.py.

Next: 10. Debugging

docs.title: 10. Debugging
docs.text:
In this lesson

You will learn to:

  • run headed to watch a script work, and outline elements with locator.highlight()
  • stop a run with page.pause() and look around
  • record a trace with context.tracing and open it with steero show-trace
  • export a trace as one HTML file to attach to a bug report
  • record a video of a page and save it
  • read steero's errors (timeouts, strictness, failed assertions) and find the cause quickly

Time: about 40 minutes. Before this: 09. The pytest plugin. Code: examples/course/10-debugging/

Sooner or later a script fails and the reason is not obvious: it worked yesterday, or it works on your machine and not on the build server. This lesson gives you four tools, from the quickest to the most thorough: watch the run, stop it and look, record a trace you can replay step by step, and record a video. It ends with how to read the error message, which is where you should always start.

docs.title: Watch it run
docs.text:
The first thing to try is to see what the browser sees. Launch headed:

with launch("chrome", headless=False) as browser:
    ...

For the course examples, set STEERO_COURSE_HEADED=1 (lesson 01); for a pytest suite, pass --headed or --steero-headed (lesson 09).

A headed script runs at full speed, which is often too fast to follow. Two helpers make it easier to see where it is:

fields = page.get_by_role("textbox")
fields.highlight(seconds=3)  # outline every element the locator matches, for 3 seconds

highlight() draws an outline around every element the locator matches right now, and returns at once. The outline never intercepts clicks, so the script carries on underneath it. It is the fastest way to answer "what does this locator actually find?": if the outline is on the wrong element, or on two elements, you know where the problem is.

docs.title: Slow motion
docs.text:
To follow a headed run by eye, launch with slow_mo: steero waits that many seconds before every action (goto, click, fill, press ...).

with launch("chrome", headless=False, slow_mo=0.5) as browser:  # half a second per action
    ...

With the pytest plugin, --slowmo 500 does the same (it takes milliseconds, as in pytest-playwright). Slow motion only helps you watch; to look closely at one moment, stop there with page.pause(), or record a trace and step through it afterwards.

Coming from Playwright

slow_mo is in seconds here, like every steero time: Playwright's slow_mo=50 is slow_mo=0.05.

docs.title: Pause
docs.text:
page.pause() stops the script until you press Enter in the terminal. While it waits, the browser is yours: click around, open its developer tools (F12), inspect the element your locator should have found.

page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
page.pause()  # look at the form, then press Enter to carry on
page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()

In a headless run there is no window to look at, so pause() logs a warning and returns at once instead of waiting for input that nobody can usefully give. That means a forgotten pause() can never hang a test run on a build server. You see the warning only if logging is switched on, for example with logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING).

Coming from Selenium

The usual Selenium trick is a breakpoint or an input() in the test. page.pause() is the same idea, with the headless case handled for you.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
A trace is a recording of everything a browser context did, saved as one zip file: every action with its locator, timing and error; a screenshot before and after each action; a snapshot of the page's HTML after each action; console messages, page errors, navigations and network requests. You can open it after the run, on another machine, days later.

Tracing belongs to a context. Start it before the actions you want, stop it with a path:

context = browser.new_context()
context.tracing.start(screenshots=True, snapshots=True, sources=True)
page = context.new_page()
...                                   # everything here is recorded
context.tracing.stop(path="trace.zip")
Option Default Adds screenshots True a picture after each action, and before it when the page changed snapshots True the page's HTML after each action, rendered without scripts sources False the line of your script that ran each action, and the script itself title, name none a title for the viewer, a short name stored in the trace

stop() without a path throws the recording away. While tracing is off it costs nothing; while it is on, each action takes a few milliseconds longer.

Chunks split one tracing session into several files, for example one per test:

context.tracing.start()                       # opens the first chunk
...
context.tracing.stop_chunk(path="step-1.zip")  # saves it; tracing stays on
context.tracing.start_chunk()
...
context.tracing.stop_chunk(path="step-2.zip")
context.tracing.stop()

You rarely need to write this yourself in a test suite: --tracing retain-on-failure makes the pytest plugin trace every test and keep trace.zip only for those that failed.

docs.title: The trace viewer
docs.text:
Open a trace with the steero command:

steero show-trace trace.zip

serving trace.zip at http://127.0.0.1:54123/ (Ctrl+C to stop)

It starts a small local server (on 127.0.0.1 only), opens the viewer in your web browser, and runs until you press Ctrl+C. Add --no-open to print the address without opening a browser, and --port 9323 to choose the port.

The viewer is one page:

  • the action list down the side: each action with its locator and duration, and failed actions marked with their error;
  • a timeline filmstrip of screenshots across the top;
  • for the selected action, the before and after screenshots and the DOM snapshot, which is the page's real HTML at that moment: you can inspect it to see why a locator did or did not match;
  • tabs for the console, the network requests, page errors and the source line that ran the action.

To attach a trace to a bug report, export it as a single HTML file that opens in any browser with no server and no steero install:

steero show-trace --html bug-1234.html trace.zip

wrote bug-1234.html

A trace holds what the page held

A trace contains screenshots, page HTML, console output and request headers. steero redacts text typed into password fields (and fields whose locator mentions a password, token or PIN), never writes password values into snapshots, and replaces Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie header values with <redacted>. Everything else is recorded as it was. Share a trace only where its contents may go.

See the tracing guide for the file format and the full option list.

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
A video is less detailed than a trace but easier to show someone. Ask for it when you create the context, then save it after the page is closed:

context = browser.new_context(record_video_dir="videos", record_video_size={"width": 800, "height": 500})
page = context.new_page()
...
video = page.video          # None when the context was not recording
page.close()                # closing the page finishes the recording
print(video.path())
video.save_as("sign-in.webm")

Every page of the context is recorded into record_video_dir. video.path() and save_as() wait until the recording is finished, so call them after page.close() (or after context.close()).

Browser support

The two browsers record video differently, and the file you get can differ:

  • Firefox records the page itself (a BiDi screencast) and writes a .webm.
  • Chrome has no screencast over BiDi yet, so steero takes screenshots, five a second, and encodes them with ffmpeg when ffmpeg is on your PATH, giving a .webm. Without ffmpeg the video is saved as <id>.frames.zip, a set of frames that steero show-trace plays, and steero logs one warning.

So a script that copies the video should keep the suffix it was given (video.path().suffixes) rather than assume .webm.

docs.title: Reading errors
docs.text:
Before any of the tools above, read the error. steero's messages are written to tell you the cause, and they have a fixed shape: the action, the locator, how long it waited, and the last reason it could not go on.

click get_by_role('button', name='Sign out'): timed out after 2 s: no element matches

The reason at the end is the part to read:

Error ends with It means Look at no element matches the locator found nothing the text, role or label in the locator against the page (highlight(), or the trace's DOM snapshot) element is not visible found, but hidden whether the page shows it yet; a menu or tab that must be opened first element is disabled found, but disabled what enables it: a field still empty, a request still running element is not stable (still moving) found, but animating an animation or a layout that keeps shifting element is covered by <div#overlay> something is on top a dialog, a cookie banner or a loading overlay matched 3 elements; use .first, .nth() or a more specific locator (a StrictModeViolation) the locator is ambiguous make it more specific (lesson 02) expected 'X', got 'Y' after 5 s (an AssertionError from expect) the page never reached the state Y is what it really showed: often the answer self-healing refused: ... a healing locator would not guess lesson 12

Two habits help. Read the last value seen in a failed assertion: "got ''" means the thing never happened at all, "got 'Signing in...'" means it was still on its way. And notice which action failed: if a click times out with "no element matches" straight after a navigation, the page may simply be a different page than you think, which the trace will show you.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
This script signs in with tracing on, then tries to click a "Sign out" button that does not exist, so the trace holds a failed action after four that worked. It saves trace.zip and exports it with steero show-trace --html, running the command through python -m steero so it uses the same Python as the script. Both files go to a steero-course folder in your temporary directory.

"""Lesson 10: record a trace of a sign-in where one step fails, and export it as one HTML file.

Signs in with tracing on, then clicks a button that does not exist, so the trace holds a failed
action next to the ones that worked. The trace is saved as ``trace.zip`` and exported with
``steero show-trace --html`` to ``trace.html``, which opens in any browser with no server.

    python examples/course/10-debugging/example_trace_failure.py
    steero show-trace <the trace.zip path it prints>

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from steero import SteeroTimeoutError
from steero.sync_api import expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "10-debugging"


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    trace = OUT / "trace.zip"
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        context = browser.new_context()
        context.tracing.start(title="sign in, then a missing button", screenshots=True, snapshots=True,
                              sources=True)
        page = context.new_page()
        page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
        page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
        page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
        try:
            page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign out").click(timeout=2)  # there is no such button
        except SteeroTimeoutError as error:
            print("Failed as planned:", error)
        context.tracing.stop(path=trace)
        context.close()
    print("Trace:", trace)

    # The same as typing: steero show-trace --html trace.html trace.zip
    html = OUT / "trace.html"
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "steero", "show-trace", "--html", str(html), str(trace)], check=True)
    print("Open this file in any browser:", html)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

python examples/course/10-debugging/example_trace_failure.py

Failed as planned: click get_by_role('button', name='Sign out'): timed out after 2 s: no element matches
Trace: C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Temp\steero-course\10-debugging\trace.zip
wrote C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Temp\steero-course\10-debugging\trace.html
Open this file in any browser: C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Temp\steero-course\10-debugging\trace.html

Open trace.html. The last action, the click, is marked as failed with the same message. Select it and look at its DOM snapshot: the form, the welcome message, and no "Sign out" button anywhere. Then open the trace live with steero show-trace and the path it printed.

A second example shows highlight() and pause(). Run it headed to see the outline and to have the script stop until you press Enter; headless, it prints the warning and finishes:

"""Lesson 10: outline an element with ``highlight()`` and stop the script with ``page.pause()``.

Headless (the default), ``pause()`` logs a warning and carries on, so the script finishes. Run it
headed to see the outline and to have the script wait for Enter in the terminal:

    python examples/course/10-debugging/example_highlight_and_pause.py
    STEERO_COURSE_HEADED=1 python examples/course/10-debugging/example_highlight_and_pause.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import logging
import os

from steero.sync_api import expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def main() -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)  # so pause()'s headless warning is printed
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        page = browser.new_page()
        page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")

        fields = page.get_by_role("textbox")
        print("Text boxes on the page:", fields.count())
        fields.highlight(seconds=3)  # outlines every match for 3 seconds; it never blocks a click

        page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
        page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
        page.pause()  # headed: waits for Enter. Headless: a warning, then on we go.

        page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
        print("Signed in")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Text boxes on the page: 2
WARNING:steero.page:page.pause() ignored: the browser is headless (launch with headless=False)
Signed in

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text: Run each solution from the repository root with the practice site running.

docs.title: Exercise 1: one trace per step
docs.text:
Sign in with tracing on, but save the filling in and the submitting as two separate trace files, using chunks. Print how many actions each file holds and how big it is.

Solution 
"""Lesson 10, exercise 1: one tracing session, one trace file per step, using chunks.

``start()`` opens the first chunk; ``stop_chunk(path)`` saves it and keeps tracing on, and
``start_chunk()`` opens the next. The script prints how many actions and bytes each file holds.

    python examples/course/10-debugging/solution_1_trace_chunks.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import steero.tracing
from steero.sync_api import expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "10-debugging" / "chunks"


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        context = browser.new_context()
        page = context.new_page()

        context.tracing.start(name="fill-in")  # opens the first chunk
        page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
        page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
        page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
        first = context.tracing.stop_chunk(path=OUT / "1-fill-in.zip")

        context.tracing.start_chunk(name="submit")
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
        second = context.tracing.stop_chunk(path=OUT / "2-submit.zip")

        context.tracing.stop()  # no chunk is open any more, so there is nothing to save
        context.close()

    for path in (first, second):
        assert path is not None
        actions = steero.tracing.load(path).document["actions"]
        print(f"{path.name}: {len(actions)} actions, {path.stat().st_size:,} bytes:",
              ", ".join(a["name"] for a in actions))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1-fill-in.zip: 3 actions, 67,478 bytes: goto, fill, fill
2-submit.zip: 1 actions, 40,101 bytes: click

expect(...) is not an action, so it is not in the list; it is the check that the submit worked. The final stop() has nothing left to save because the last chunk was already closed.

docs.title: Exercise 2: a video of signing in
docs.text:
Record a video of the sign-in flow at 800 by 500, save a copy named after the browser, and print both paths. Run it in Chrome and in Firefox and compare.

Solution 
"""Lesson 10, exercise 2: record a video of the sign-in flow and print where it was saved.

Firefox writes a ``.webm`` itself. Chrome's frames are encoded to ``.webm`` with ffmpeg when it
is on PATH; without ffmpeg the video is a ``.frames.zip`` that ``steero show-trace`` plays.

    python examples/course/10-debugging/solution_2_video.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from steero.sync_api import expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "10-debugging" / "video"


def main() -> None:
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        context = browser.new_context(record_video_dir=OUT, record_video_size={"width": 800, "height": 500})
        page = context.new_page()
        page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
        page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
        page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")

        video = page.video
        assert video is not None, "the context was created with record_video_dir"
        page.close()  # closing the page finishes the recording
        path = video.path()
        copy = video.save_as(OUT / f"sign-in-{BROWSER}{''.join(path.suffixes)}")
        context.close()

    print("Recorded:", path)
    print("Saved a copy as:", copy, f"({copy.stat().st_size:,} bytes)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Recorded: ...\video\64405624a0d14625895fe87003365243.webm
Saved a copy as: ...\video\sign-in-chrome.webm (23,078 bytes)

The copy keeps the suffixes of the original, so on Chrome without ffmpeg it is correctly named .frames.zip rather than a .webm that is not one.

docs.title: Exercise 3: read a trace from code
docs.text:
A trace is a zip with a JSON document inside, and steero.tracing.load(path) reads it. Record a short trace with one failing action, load it, and print each action's name, target, duration in seconds and error type.

Hint: the actions are in trace.document["actions"]; each one has name, target, duration and error (None, or a dict with type and message).

Solution 
"""Lesson 10, exercise 3: read a trace from code and print each action with its duration.

Records a short trace (one action fails on purpose), then opens it with ``steero.tracing.load``
and prints a table: action, target, seconds, and the error if there was one.

    python examples/course/10-debugging/solution_3_read_trace.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import steero.tracing
from steero import SteeroTimeoutError
from steero.sync_api import launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "10-debugging"


def record(path: Path) -> None:
    """Sign in with tracing on; the last click fails after 1 second."""
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        context = browser.new_context()
        context.tracing.start(screenshots=False, snapshots=False)  # actions only: a small file
        page = context.new_page()
        page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
        page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
        page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
        try:
            page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign out").click(timeout=1)
        except SteeroTimeoutError:
            pass  # the point is to see it in the trace
        context.tracing.stop(path=path)
        context.close()


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / "read-me.zip"
    record(path)

    trace = steero.tracing.load(path)
    print(f"{trace.document['meta']['browser']}: {len(trace.document['actions'])} actions")
    for action in trace.document["actions"]:
        error = action["error"]["type"] if action["error"] else ""
        print(f"  {action['name']:6} {action['target'] or '':45} {action['duration']:6.3f} s  {error}")
    failed = [a for a in trace.document["actions"] if a["error"]]
    assert len(failed) == 1 and failed[0]["error"]["type"] == "SteeroTimeoutError"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

chrome: 5 actions
  goto                                                  0.132 s
  fill   get_by_label('User name')                      0.088 s
  fill   get_by_label('Password')                       0.045 s
  click  get_by_role('button', name='Sign in')          0.133 s
  click  get_by_role('button', name='Sign out')         1.036 s  SteeroTimeoutError

Reading traces from code is handy on a build server: a few lines can list the slowest actions of every failed test without opening a viewer.

docs.title: Exercise 4: find the cause from the message
docs.text:
Each of these three fragments runs on the sign-in page and fails. Before running them, read each one and predict the error. Then run them and check your diagnosis against the message.

page.locator("input").fill("ada", timeout=2)                          # 1
page.get_by_label("Username").fill("ada", timeout=2)                   # 2
page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")                             # 3
page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
expect(page.get_by_role("status"), timeout=2).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
Solution 
"""Lesson 10, exercise 4: three broken scripts, and what each error message says is wrong.

Each function is one of the lesson's broken scripts. The script runs all three, catches the
error each one raises and prints it, so you can compare it with your diagnosis.

    python examples/course/10-debugging/solution_4_read_errors.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
from collections.abc import Callable

from steero import SteeroTimeoutError, StrictModeViolation
from steero.sync_api import Page, expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def broken_1(page: Page) -> None:
    page.locator("input").fill("ada", timeout=2)


def broken_2(page: Page) -> None:
    page.get_by_label("Username").fill("ada", timeout=2)


def broken_3(page: Page) -> None:
    page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
    page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
    expect(page.get_by_role("status"), timeout=2).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")


CASES: list[tuple[Callable[[Page], None], type[Exception], str]] = [
    (broken_1, StrictModeViolation, "the locator matches three inputs: say which one"),
    (broken_2, SteeroTimeoutError, "no element matches: the label is 'User name', with a space"),
    (broken_3, AssertionError, "the status stayed empty: nobody clicked Sign in"),
]


def main() -> None:
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        for script, expected, diagnosis in CASES:
            context = browser.new_context()  # a clean start for each broken script
            page = context.new_page()
            page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
            try:
                script(page)
            except expected as error:
                print(f"{script.__name__}: {type(error).__name__}")
                print(f"    {error}")
                print(f"    cause: {diagnosis}")
            else:
                raise AssertionError(f"{script.__name__} was expected to fail")
            context.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

broken_1: StrictModeViolation
    locator('input') matched 3 elements; use .first, .nth() or a more specific locator
broken_2: SteeroTimeoutError
    fill get_by_label('Username'): timed out after 2 s: no element matches
broken_3: AssertionError
    expect(get_by_role('status')).to_have_text: expected 'Welcome, ada', got '' after 2 s

The first fails at once: being ambiguous is not something waiting can fix. The second waits the full 2 seconds, because the element might still appear. The third says "got ''": the welcome never started, so look for the step that should have caused it, here the missing click.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Common mistakes

  • page.pause() does nothing. The browser is headless; pause() only waits in a headed run. Launch with headless=False (or STEERO_COURSE_HEADED=1, --headed).
  • SteeroError: tracing is already started on this context. start() was called twice. Call stop() first, or use stop_chunk() and start_chunk() to split a recording.
  • The trace file is missing. stop() was called without a path, which discards the recording, or the script failed before stop(). Put stop(path=...) in a finally, or let the pytest plugin do it with --tracing retain-on-failure.
  • steero show-trace says the file is not a steero trace. It reads steero traces and steero frame sets; it cannot open a Playwright trace, and Playwright's viewer cannot open a steero trace.
  • Chrome's video is a .frames.zip. ffmpeg is not on PATH. Install it, or play the frame set with steero show-trace.
  • video.path() blocks or the file is empty. The page is still open. Close the page (or the context) first: that is what finishes the recording.
  • Sharing a trace with secrets in it. Passwords and auth headers are redacted, but page text, other headers and console output are not. Check before attaching one to a public issue.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• Run headed and use highlight() to see what a locator finds; page.pause() stops a headed run until Enter and is ignored headless.
  • context.tracing.start() and stop(path="trace.zip") record actions, screenshots, DOM snapshots, console and network; chunks split one session into several files.
  • steero show-trace trace.zip opens the viewer; --html out.html writes one file to attach to a bug.
  • new_context(record_video_dir=...) records video; Firefox writes .webm itself, Chrome needs ffmpeg for .webm and otherwise saves a .frames.zip.
  • Read the error first: action, locator, time waited and the last reason.

Next: 11. Recording with codegen

docs.title: 11. Recording with codegen
docs.text:
In this lesson

You will learn to:

  • record a script with steero codegen in Chrome or Firefox
  • choose a target (sync script, async script or pytest test) and write it to a file
  • use the toolbar: pause, pick a locator, add assertions
  • explain how the recorder chooses locators, and ask it from code with generate_locator
  • tidy a recording into a good test

Time: about 25 minutes. Before this: 10. Debugging. Code: examples/course/11-codegen/

Writing the first draft of a test by hand means looking up every label and role on the page. codegen does that part for you: you use the page in a real browser, and steero writes the script that does the same thing, with the user-facing locators you learned in lesson 02. What it cannot do is decide what your test should check. This lesson covers both halves.

docs.title: Recording
docs.text:
Start the practice site, then:

steero codegen http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html

A visible Chrome window opens on the sign-in page, with a small toolbar at the bottom. Type a user name and a password, click Sign in, and watch the terminal: the script appears as you go. Close the window (or press Ctrl+C in the terminal) to finish. Either way the browser is shut down and its profile deleted.

"""Recorded with steero codegen."""

from steero.sync_api import launch

with launch("chrome", headless=False) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html")
    page.get_by_test_id("username").fill("ada")
    page.get_by_test_id("password").fill("lovelace")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()

Typing is recorded as one fill() per field with its final value, not one line per key. The script runs unmodified: save it and run it with python.

The options:

Option Meaning url the first page, recorded as page.goto(...); optional --browser chrome\|firefox which browser to record in (default chrome) --target python a sync script (the default) --target python-async an async with steero.launch(...) script --target python-pytest a pytest test using the steero_page fixture (lesson 09) --output FILE also write the script to FILE, rewritten after every change --viewport 1280x720 the page's viewport size --device "iPhone 13" the viewport of a common device (only its size is applied) --test-id-attribute data-qa the attribute get_by_test_id reads (default data-testid)

For a test you will keep, record straight into a test file:

steero codegen http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html --target python-pytest --output test_sign_in.py

Coming from Playwright

steero codegen is the counterpart of playwright codegen, with the same idea of targets and a toolbar. It records with the stock browser you have installed, and the script it writes uses steero's API (seconds for timeouts, steero_page in pytest). There is no separate inspector window: the script streams to the terminal and to --output.

Browser support

Recording works the same in Chrome and Firefox: the recorder is a script steero installs in every frame over WebDriver BiDi, not a browser extension. A script recorded in one browser runs in the other once you change the name in launch(...) (or pass --browser to pytest).

docs.title: The toolbar
docs.text:
The toolbar at the bottom of the page controls the recorder. It sits in a closed shadow root, so the page's CSS cannot restyle it, its buttons are invisible to locators, and its clicks never reach the page's own event handlers.

  • Pause / Record stops and resumes recording. Use it to get the page into the right state (close a cookie banner, scroll to a section) without those steps ending up in the script.
  • Pick locator shows, as you move the pointer, the locator the recorder would write for the element under it. Clicking prints it in the terminal (and copies it to the clipboard when the browser allows); the click does not reach the page. This is the quickest way to get a good locator for a test you are writing by hand.
  • Assert visible, Assert text and Assert value: click one, then click an element, and the recorder adds expect(...).to_be_visible(), to_contain_text(...) or to_have_value(...) for it, instead of a click. Escape leaves these modes.

docs.title: How locators are chosen
docs.text:
For each action, the page proposes candidate locators for the element, and steero counts each candidate with its own selector engine. A locator is written only if steero resolves it to exactly that element, so a recorded locator is never ambiguous and never relies on a difference between the browser's idea of a role and steero's. The first unique candidate wins, in this order:

  1. get_by_test_id
  2. get_by_role(role, name=...)
  3. get_by_label
  4. get_by_placeholder
  5. get_by_alt_text
  6. get_by_text
  7. get_by_title
  8. get_by_role(role) without a name
  9. short CSS: an id, then stable attributes
  10. .first or .nth(i) on the best candidate, as a last resort

Ids and class names that look generated by a framework or a build (css-1x2y3z, :r1:, ember1234, hashes) are never used, because they change from one build to the next.

That order explains the recording above: the sign-in form's inputs have data-testid attributes, so they are recorded as get_by_test_id("username"), while the button has none and is recorded by its role and name.

docs.title: Locators from code
docs.text:
The same choice is available as a coroutine, for tools and for your own curiosity:

from steero.codegen import generate_locator

code = await generate_locator(page.locator("#sign-in"))  # 'page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in")'

It takes any locator that matches exactly one element and returns source code. Pass test_id_attribute= to match your project's attribute, and receiver= to start the chain with another variable name than page.

docs.title: From a recording to a test
docs.text:
A recording is a first draft. Before it becomes a test, go through it once:

  1. Remove the noise. Clicks that only focused a field, a scroll that does not matter, a step you made by mistake. (Pause the recorder next time.)
  2. Add the checks. The recorder writes what you did, not what should be true afterwards. A recorded sign-in clicks the button and stops; the test must also assert the welcome message. Use the toolbar's assert buttons, or write expect(...) yourself.
  3. Prefer the assertion you mean. An Assert text click locates the element by what it is (a test id, a role, a label, CSS) rather than by the text it checks, so the status line here becomes expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_contain_text("Welcome, ada"). When the element's own text is the only way to find it, the recorder writes to_be_visible() on get_by_text(...) instead, because to_contain_text of the same text could never fail. Tighten to_contain_text to to_have_text when the whole text matters.
  4. Replace literal data. The user name you typed, today's date, an order number: move them into variables or fixtures, and the URL into --base-url (lesson 09).
  5. Name it. test_recorded becomes test_sign_in_shows_welcome.

The tidied version of the recording above:

from steero.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_sign_in_shows_welcome(steero_page: Page) -> None:
    steero_page.goto("login.html")
    steero_page.get_by_test_id("username").fill("ada")
    steero_page.get_by_test_id("password").fill("lovelace")
    steero_page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
    expect(steero_page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
What is recorded: clicks (with modifier keys) and double clicks; typing; Enter, Tab, Escape and shortcuts as press(); checking, select_option and file uploads (file names only); navigations you make from the address bar; popups and new tabs; actions inside iframes, through frame_locator(...) chains.

What is not recorded:

  • hover, drag and drop, scrolling and right clicks. Add them by hand (lesson 03).
  • The files themselves for an upload: the script names the files, and they must exist next to it.
  • Waits. The recorder does not know that you waited for a message before clicking on; the auto-waiting of actions covers most of this, and assertions cover the rest.

Navigations are told apart by timing: a navigation shortly after a click or a key press is left to that action, and one that happens on its own a few seconds after your last action is recorded as a goto. A page that redirects itself late may therefore get an extra goto line; delete it.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
steero codegen needs you at the keyboard, so the course cannot run it as it is. Instead, the example uses the same Recorder class the command uses, headless, and drives the page with steero's own actions. Those reach the page as real input, exactly as your clicks would, so the recorder cannot tell the difference. The script records signing in, prints what was recorded, saves it to your temporary directory and runs it in a fresh Python process, unmodified.

Notice that it drives the page with brittle #id locators, and the recording comes out with good ones: the recorder chooses its own locators from the element, not from how you found it.

"""Lesson 11: record signing in with the codegen recorder, then run the script it wrote.

``steero codegen`` is interactive: you click in a visible browser. To run unattended, this
example uses the same ``Recorder`` headless and drives the page with steero's own actions, which
reach the page as real input, exactly like yours. The script it records is saved to your
temporary directory and run in a new Python process, unmodified.

    python examples/course/11-codegen/example_record_sign_in.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import asyncio
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import steero
from steero.codegen import Recorder

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "11-codegen"


async def record() -> str:
    """What you would do by hand after ``steero codegen <url>/login.html``."""
    async with steero.launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        recorder = Recorder(browser, target="python", headless=True)
        try:
            page = await recorder.start(BASE_URL + "login.html")
            await page.locator("#username").fill("ada")
            await page.locator("#password").fill("lovelace")
            await page.locator("#sign-in").click()
            await steero.expect(page.locator("#status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
        finally:
            script = await recorder.stop()
    return script


def main() -> None:
    script = asyncio.run(record())
    print(script, flush=True)
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / "recorded_sign_in.py"
    path.write_text(script, encoding="utf-8")
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(path)], check=True)
    print("Saved and replayed:", path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Recorded with steero codegen."""

from steero.sync_api import launch

with launch("chrome", headless=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html")
    page.get_by_test_id("username").fill("ada")
    page.get_by_test_id("password").fill("lovelace")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()

Saved and replayed: C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Temp\steero-course\11-codegen\recorded_sign_in.py

Now record the same thing yourself with steero codegen http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html and compare: the only difference should be headless=False.

A second example asks generate_locator about every control on the sign-in form:

"""Lesson 11: which locator would the recorder write for each control on the sign-in form?

``generate_locator`` runs the recorder's own choice (test id, then role and name, then label ...)
on any element you point at, so you can see its decisions without recording anything.

    python examples/course/11-codegen/example_generate_locators.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import asyncio
import os

import steero
from steero.codegen import generate_locator

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

# The sign-in form's controls, found by id: the brittle way the recorder improves on.
CONTROLS = ["#username", "#password", "#remember", "#sign-in", "#status", "header a[href='products.html']"]


async def main() -> None:
    async with steero.launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        page = await browser.new_page()
        await page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
        for selector in CONTROLS:
            code = await generate_locator(page.locator(selector))
            print(f"{selector:32} -> {code}")

        # A different test id attribute changes the choice (this page has none called data-qa).
        code = await generate_locator(page.locator("#username"), test_id_attribute="data-qa")
        print(f"{'#username (data-qa)':32} -> {code}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

#username                        -> page.get_by_test_id("username")
#password                        -> page.get_by_test_id("password")
#remember                        -> page.get_by_role("checkbox", name="Remember me")
#sign-in                         -> page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in")
#status                          -> page.get_by_role("status")
header a[href='products.html']   -> page.get_by_role("link", name="Products")
#username (data-qa)              -> page.get_by_role("textbox", name="User name")

The last line shows the order at work: with data-qa as the test id attribute, the field has no test id, so the next rule, role and name, wins.

docs.title: Exercise 1: record a pytest test
docs.text:
Record signing in on the practice site as a pytest test, into a file, and run it with pytest.

steero codegen http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html --target python-pytest --output test_recorded.py
pytest test_recorded.py
Solution

The solution does the same unattended, with Recorder(..., target="python-pytest"), and then runs the recorded file with pytest:

"""Lesson 11, exercise 1: record signing in as a pytest test, then run the test with pytest.

The same as ``steero codegen <url>/login.html --target python-pytest --output test_recorded.py``,
driven headless. The recorded test uses the ``steero_page`` fixture from lesson 09.

import steero

# course: timeout=180

def main() -> None:

    print("The recorded test passed:", test_file)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def test_recorded(steero_page: Page) -> None:
    page = steero_page
    page.goto("http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html")
    page.get_by_test_id("username").fill("grace")
    page.get_by_test_id("password").fill("hopper")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()

It passes, but it checks nothing: it would pass even if signing in were broken. That is what exercise 2 is for.

docs.title: Exercise 2: an assertion from the toolbar
docs.text:
Record signing in again. When the welcome message appears, click Assert text in the toolbar and then click the message. Check that the script gained an expect(...) line, and run it.

Solution

The toolbar's button switches the recorder's mode; from code that is set_mode("assert-text"):

"""Lesson 11, exercise 2: add a text assertion while recording, the way the toolbar does.

Clicking the toolbar's **Assert text** button switches the recorder to ``assert-text`` mode; the
next click on the page adds an assertion instead of a click. ``set_mode`` is what that button
calls. The recorded script is then replayed, so the assertion is checked for real.

    python examples/course/11-codegen/solution_2_assert_text.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
Modified: Nov-07-2026 (the assertion target is structural now)
"""

import asyncio
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import steero
from steero.codegen import Recorder

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

OUT = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "steero-course" / "11-codegen"


async def record() -> str:
    async with steero.launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        recorder = Recorder(browser, headless=True)
        try:
            page = await recorder.start(BASE_URL + "login.html")
            await page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
            await page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
            await page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
            status = page.get_by_role("status")
            await steero.expect(status).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")  # wait, as you would by eye

            await recorder.set_mode("assert-text")  # the Assert text button
            await status.click()  # this click becomes an assertion, and never reaches the page
        finally:
            script = await recorder.stop()
    return script


def main() -> None:
    script = asyncio.run(record())
    print(script, flush=True)
    # The recorder finds the status line by its role, not by the text it checks.
    assert 'expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_contain_text("Welcome, ada")' in script
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / "recorded_with_assertion.py"
    path.write_text(script, encoding="utf-8")
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(path)], check=True)
    print("Replayed, assertion included:", path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_contain_text("Welcome, ada")

The assertion finds the message by its role, not by the text it checks, so it fails if the status line shows anything else. The script imports expect because it now has an assertion; a recording without one imports only launch.

docs.title: Exercise 3: what would the recorder write?
docs.text:
Open /testsite/form.html and print the locator the recorder would choose for at least five of its elements, found by CSS: the user name field, the password, the search box, the country list, the submit button, the logo and the second list item.

Solution 
"""Lesson 11, exercise 3: the locators the recorder would choose on steero's test form.

Points ``generate_locator`` at seven elements of ``/testsite/form.html`` by CSS and prints the
user-facing locator the recorder would write instead.

import asyncio
import os

import steero
from steero.codegen import generate_locator

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")

#pass                    -> page.get_by_role("textbox", name="Password")
#search                  -> page.get_by_role("searchbox", name="Search")
#country                 -> page.get_by_role("combobox", name="Country")
button[type=submit]      -> page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in")
img                      -> page.get_by_role("img", name="Company logo")
