docs.title: Exercise 3: your own client, Firefox
docs.text:
Add steero to the configuration of an MCP client you use, with --browser firefox and --headed, restart the client, and ask it to "open http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html, sign in as ada with any password and tell me what the page says". Watch the window while it works.

To check a configuration before you hand it to a client, write it to a file and start the command it names yourself. The solution does that for Firefox, and falls back to python -m steero with the full path to Python when steero is not on PATH.

Solution 
"""Lesson 14, exercise 3: write an MCP client configuration for Firefox, then check it works.

An MCP client (an IDE, a desktop assistant, an agent framework) starts the server from a
``command`` and ``args`` entry. This script writes that entry to ``mcp.json``, then starts
exactly that command and checks the handshake and one tool call, which is what the client
will do. When ``steero`` is not on PATH (a virtual environment that is not activated), it
writes the same server as ``python -m steero`` with the full path to Python.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

# course: browsers=firefox

import json
import os
import shutil
import sys

from mcp_client import McpClient

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "firefox")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def server_entry() -> dict[str, object]:
    """The ``mcpServers`` entry for steero driving Firefox."""
    args = ["mcp", "--browser", "firefox"] + ([] if HEADLESS else ["--headed"])
    steero = shutil.which("steero")
    if steero:
        return {"command": steero, "args": args}
    return {"command": sys.executable, "args": ["-m", "steero", *args]}


def main() -> None:
    config = {"mcpServers": {"steero": server_entry()}}
    with open("mcp.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        json.dump(config, file, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(config, indent=2))

    # Read it back and start the server the way a client would.
    with open("mcp.json", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        entry = json.load(file)["mcpServers"]["steero"]
    with McpClient(command=[entry["command"], *entry["args"]]) as client:
        client.initialize()
        snapshot = client.text("browser_navigate", url=BASE_URL + "login.html")
        assert "Page: Sign in - steero practice site" in snapshot, snapshot
        agent = client.text("browser_evaluate", script="navigator.userAgent")
        assert "Firefox" in agent, agent
        print("The configuration starts a working server in Firefox")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

If your client reports that the server "closed" or "failed to start", run the configured command by hand in a terminal: an error such as a missing browser is printed there, on standard error, where clients often hide it.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Common mistakes

  • Printing to standard output in the server process. stdout carries the protocol, so any stray line breaks the client's parser. steero logs to stderr only; keep it that way in anything you wrap around it.
  • Reusing refs from an old snapshot. Each snapshot numbers the elements again, and after a page changes an old ref may point at nothing (isError: true, a timeout). Take a new snapshot, or use the one an action returns.
  • The client cannot start steero. The client runs outside your virtual environment. Put the full path to steero (or to the environment's Python with -m steero) in the configuration.
  • Waiting forever for a reply. Every request needs an id, and a notification gets no reply at all. Give each read a deadline, as mcp_client.py does.
  • Asking for a browser by a name steero does not know. --browser takes chrome, edge or firefox; anything else is a usage error and the server exits.
  • Pointing an agent at a real site on the first try. Start with the practice site and --headed, and review what it does before you trust it with more.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• steero mcp is an MCP server on stdio that gives an AI agent a fresh Chrome or Firefox.
  • The agent acts with your network access: trusted agents only, watch it, review it.
  • A client is configured with "command": "steero", "args": ["mcp", "--browser", "firefox"].
  • Snapshots give refs (e1, e2 ...); actions take a ref, auto-wait like a test, and report failures as isError results.
  • Any program can be the client: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, one JSON line each.

Next: 15. Migrating from Playwright

docs.title: 15. Migrating from Playwright
docs.text:
In this lesson

You will learn to:

  • run an existing Playwright for Python script on steero by changing only the import
  • keep pytest-playwright fixture names with -p steero.compat.playwright.pytest
  • know what the compatibility layer translates (milliseconds, wait_until, selector shortcuts) and what raises UnsupportedFeature
  • move code to steero's native API step by step: seconds, steero.launch, locators, steero_page
  • decide when to stay on the layer and when to move

Time: about 40 minutes. Before this: 14. AI agents with MCP. Code: examples/course/15-migrating-from-playwright/

If you have Playwright scripts or a pytest-playwright suite already, you do not have to rewrite them before trying steero. A compatibility layer accepts Playwright's API, translates it, and runs it on stock Chrome and Firefox. This lesson shows what that layer does, where it stops, and how to move to steero's own API when you are ready.

Milliseconds in this lesson

Everywhere else in the course, timeouts are seconds. Code that imports from steero.compat.playwright keeps Playwright's milliseconds: timeout=2000 there is two seconds. Each snippet below says which API it uses.

docs.title: Change only the import
docs.text:
The layer lives in steero.compat.playwright, with the same module names as Playwright:

# before
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, expect
# after
from steero.compat.playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, expect

The async API is steero.compat.playwright.async_api (async_playwright). Everything after the import stays as it was: sync_playwright() starts the layer, p.chromium launches stock Chrome, p.firefox launches stock Firefox, p.chromium.launch(channel="msedge") launches Edge. p.webkit exists, but launching it raises, because Safari has no WebDriver BiDi. The layer never imports the real playwright package, so you can install both side by side and switch one import at a time.

docs.title: What is translated
docs.text:
The layer turns Playwright's conventions into steero calls:

Playwright writes The layer does timeout=2000, set_default_timeout(10000), slow_mo=50, expect(..., timeout=3000) divides by 1000: steero gets seconds. timeout=0 means no limit, as in Playwright wait_until="load", "domcontentloaded", "commit", "networkidle" steero's complete, interactive, none; networkidle waits for 500 ms with no requests response = page.goto(url) returns the main Response (.ok, .status, .json()) page.click(selector), fill, text_content, is_visible, query_selector ... builds a locator for the first match and acts on it element handles (query_selector, element_handle()) locators, which find the element again on each use route.fulfill(json=...), route.abort(), handlers taking (route) or (route, request) steero's routing expect_response, expect_request, expect_download, expect_console_message ... steero's event waiters, with predicate= Error, TimeoutError steero.SteeroError, steero.SteeroTimeoutError

The migration guide has the complete list.

docs.title: What is not
docs.text:
Anything Playwright has and steero does not raises UnsupportedFeature, from steero.compat.playwright. Its message names the missing piece and links the guide, and its feature attribute holds the name:

from steero.compat.playwright import UnsupportedFeature

try:
    page.evaluate_handle("document.body")
except UnsupportedFeature as error:
    print(error.feature)   # Page.evaluate_handle

The main ones: WebKit, launch_persistent_context (steero always starts from a fresh profile), connect and connect_over_cdp, JS handles (evaluate_handle, JSHandle), route(times=), goto(referer=), and a few launch options (env=, ignore_default_args=, downloads_path=). An argument steero lacks is dropped silently only when it holds Playwright's do-nothing value (None, False, 0); any other value raises, so click(trial=True) never quietly clicks. UnsupportedFeature is a NotImplementedError; for a missing attribute it is also an AttributeError, so hasattr(page, "evaluate_handle") keeps working.

Browser support

The layer runs on everything steero drives: Chrome (both backends), Edge and Firefox. A Playwright option that maps to a Chrome-only steero option (for example is_mobile in new_context) raises UnsupportedOnBrowser in Firefox, exactly as in native steero (lesson 13).

docs.title: pytest-playwright suites
docs.text:
pytest-playwright gives tests fixtures called page, context, browser, browser_name and base_url. steero has an opt-in plugin with the same names and markers:

pytest -p steero.compat.playwright.pytest --browser chromium --browser firefox

Or put -p steero.compat.playwright.pytest in the suite's addopts, as the lesson's pw_suite/pytest.ini does. It provides page, context, new_context, browser, browser_name (chromium or firefox; Edge counts as chromium), browser_type, browser_context_args, base_url, output_path, is_chromium, is_firefox and the skip_browser, only_browser and browser_context_args markers. The objects come from the compatibility layer, so the tests keep their milliseconds.

It is not on by default: its fixture names would clash with pytest-playwright's when both are installed. For the same reason, the plain options (--browser, --base-url, --headed, --screenshot, --tracing ...) are registered only when pytest-playwright is not installed; the --steero- spellings (--steero-browser, --steero-base-url ...) always work, and the lesson's script uses those.

"""Lesson 15: tests written for pytest-playwright, run unchanged on steero's opt-in plugin.

The fixtures ``page``, ``base_url`` and ``browser_name`` and the ``skip_browser`` marker come from
``-p steero.compat.playwright.pytest`` (see ``pytest.ini``); only the import line changed.
Timeouts are milliseconds, as in Playwright.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import re

import pytest

# from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect      # before
from steero.compat.playwright.sync_api import Page, expect  # after


def test_sign_in_shows_welcome(page: Page) -> None:
    page.goto("login.html")  # relative to --base-url
    page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
    page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada", timeout=2000)


def test_empty_password_is_refused(page: Page) -> None:
    page.goto("login.html")
    page.fill("#username", "ada")
    page.click("#sign-in")
    expect(page.get_by_text("Password is required")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page).to_have_title(re.compile("Sign in"))


@pytest.mark.skip_browser("firefox")
def test_reports_chromium(page: Page, browser_name: str) -> None:
    assert browser_name == "chromium"  # Chrome and Edge both count as chromium
    page.goto("index.html")
    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="Practice site")).to_be_visible()

"""Lesson 15: run a pytest-playwright suite on steero with the opt-in plugin.

Runs ``pw_suite/`` with pytest in this process. The suite's ``pytest.ini`` turns on
``-p steero.compat.playwright.pytest``; the browser and base URL are passed as
``--steero-browser`` and ``--steero-base-url``, which always exist (the plain ``--browser``
and ``--base-url`` are taken by pytest-playwright when it is installed too).

    python examples/course/15-migrating-from-playwright/example_pytest_playwright.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

SUITE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "pw_suite"


def main() -> None:
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True  # keep __pycache__ out of the examples folder
    output = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pw-suite-")
    args = [str(SUITE), "-q", "--steero-browser", BROWSER, "--steero-base-url", BASE_URL,
            "--steero-output", output, "--steero-screenshot", "only-on-failure"]
    if not HEADLESS:
        args.append("--steero-headed")
    code = pytest.main(args)
    print(f"pytest exited {int(code)}; artifacts (if any) in {output}")
    if code != 0:
        raise SystemExit(int(code))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

...                                                                      [100%]
3 passed in 5.56s

docs.title: Moving to native steero
docs.text:
The layer is a bridge, not a destination: it adds a translation step to every call, and new steero features (self-healing, the Chrome extras, steero's own fixtures) are native only. Move a script or a test module at a time:

  1. Imports and launch. from steero.sync_api import expect, launch, then with launch("chrome") as browser: instead of sync_playwright() and p.chromium.launch().
  2. Timeouts. Divide every number by 1000: timeout=2000 becomes timeout=2. Search the file for timeout, delay, slow_mo and wait_for_timeout.
  3. Navigation. wait_until="domcontentloaded" becomes "interactive", "load" becomes "complete", "commit" becomes "none". Native goto() returns the main Response, as in Playwright (None for about:blank and other pages without one), so page.goto(url).status carries over unchanged.
  4. Selector shortcuts to locators. page.fill("#username", "ada") becomes page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada"): the same action, a locator that says what the user sees (lesson 02).
  5. Tests. Use the native plugin's steero_page fixture (or alias it as page in conftest.py, lesson 09), and drop -p steero.compat.playwright.pytest.

The migration guide's table maps the remaining names.

Coming from Selenium

There is no compatibility layer for Selenium: its model (element references, explicit waits) is too different for a faithful translation. The Selenium guide maps the concepts; the native API in this course is the target.

docs.title: Choosing
docs.text:
Stay on the layer while you evaluate, or when a large suite must keep running during a gradual move. Move to native steero for new code, and for anything that should use self-healing, MCP or the Chrome extras.

Choose steero when you need the stock browsers your users run (especially Firefox, which Playwright patches), the W3C standard protocol, or the built-in healing and MCP server. Stay with Playwright when you need WebKit, JS and element handles, persistent profiles, clients in other languages, or the maturity of a tool with years of use and a large team behind it. The comparison page says more.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
The first script is written as Playwright's documentation would write it (sync API, milliseconds, page.fill(selector), expect_response, route.fulfill(json=...)), with only the import changed. It signs in, waits for the products API and then mocks it.

"""Lesson 15: a Playwright for Python script, run on steero by changing only the import.

Everything below the import is written the way Playwright's documentation writes it:
``sync_playwright()``, ``p.chromium``, selector shortcuts such as ``page.fill(selector)``,
``wait_until=``, ``route.fulfill(json=...)``, ``expect_response`` and timeouts in
MILLISECONDS, which the compatibility layer translates.

    python examples/course/15-migrating-from-playwright/example_playwright_script.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os

# from playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright      # before
from steero.compat.playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright  # after

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

MOCKED = [{"id": 7, "name": "Mocked mug", "price": 1.0, "stock": 5}]


def main() -> None:
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser_type = p.firefox if BROWSER == "firefox" else p.chromium
        channel = "msedge" if BROWSER == "edge" else None
        browser = browser_type.launch(headless=HEADLESS, channel=channel, timeout=30000)  # 30000 ms
        page = browser.new_page()
        page.set_default_timeout(10000)  # 10 seconds, in Playwright's milliseconds

        response = page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
        assert response is not None and response.ok
        page.fill("#username", "ada")
        page.fill("#password", "lovelace")
        page.click("#sign-in")
        expect(page.locator("#status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada", timeout=2000)  # 2 seconds
        print("Signed in:", page.text_content("#status"))

        with page.expect_response("**/api/products") as response_info:
            page.goto(BASE_URL + "products.html")
        print("Products API answered", response_info.value.status)

        page.route("**/api/products", lambda route: route.fulfill(json=MOCKED))
        page.click("#reload")
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("1 products")
        print("Mocked:", page.text_content("tbody td"))
        browser.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

python examples/course/15-migrating-from-playwright/example_playwright_script.py

Signed in: Welcome, ada
Products API answered 200
Mocked: Mocked mug

The second does the same with steero's own API. Read the two side by side: the structure is the same, the numbers are a thousand times smaller, and the selectors became user-facing locators.

"""Lesson 15: the same script rewritten to steero's own API.

Compare it line by line with ``example_playwright_script.py``: no ``sync_playwright()``,
``launch("chrome")`` instead of ``p.chromium.launch()``, locators instead of selector
shortcuts, and every timeout in SECONDS.

    python examples/course/15-migrating-from-playwright/example_native_rewrite.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os

from steero.sync_api import expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

MOCKED = [{"id": 7, "name": "Mocked mug", "price": 1.0, "stock": 5}]


def main() -> None:
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS, timeout=30) as browser:  # 30 seconds
        page = browser.new_page()
        page.set_default_timeout(10)  # 10 seconds

        # steero's goto returns None, so wait for the document's response explicitly.
        # "interactive" is steero's spelling of Playwright's "domcontentloaded".
        with page.expect_response("**/login.html") as login_info:
            page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html", wait_until="interactive")
        assert login_info.value.ok
        page.get_by_label("User name").fill("ada")
        page.get_by_label("Password").fill("lovelace")
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada", timeout=2)  # 2 seconds
        print("Signed in:", page.get_by_role("status").text_content())

        with page.expect_response("**/api/products") as response_info:
            page.goto(BASE_URL + "products.html")
        print("Products API answered", response_info.value.status)

        page.route("**/api/products", lambda route: route.fulfill(json=MOCKED))
        page.get_by_role("button", name="Reload").click()
        expect(page.get_by_role("status")).to_have_text("1 products")
        print("Mocked:", page.get_by_role("cell").first.text_content())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

It prints the same three lines. The course test runs both in Chrome and Firefox, which is a good pattern for your own migration: keep the old script running until the new one passes too.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text: Run each solution from the repository root with the practice site running.

docs.title: Exercise 1: an async script, ported
docs.text:
Here is a Playwright async script. Port it to steero by changing only the import, and run it.

import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright, expect

async def main() -> None:
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch()
        context = await browser.new_context(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
        page = await context.new_page()
        await page.goto("login.html")
        await page.get_by_label("User name").fill("linus")
        await page.get_by_label("Password").fill("torvalds")
        await page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click(timeout=5000)
        await expect(page).to_have_title("Welcome - steero practice site", timeout=3000)
        await page.goto("products.html", wait_until="networkidle")
        await expect(page.locator("tbody tr")).to_have_count(3)
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())
Solution 
"""Lesson 15, exercise 1: a Playwright async script ported to steero by changing the import.

Only the import line differs from the Playwright original shown in the lesson. Timeouts
stay in milliseconds, because this is the compatibility layer.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import asyncio
import os

# from playwright.async_api import async_playwright, expect          # before
from steero.compat.playwright.async_api import async_playwright, expect  # after

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


async def main() -> None:
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser_type = p.firefox if BROWSER == "firefox" else p.chromium
        channel = "msedge" if BROWSER == "edge" else None
        browser = await browser_type.launch(headless=HEADLESS, channel=channel)
        context = await browser.new_context(base_url=BASE_URL)
        page = await context.new_page()

        await page.goto("login.html")
        await page.get_by_label("User name").fill("linus")
        await page.get_by_label("Password").fill("torvalds")
        await page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click(timeout=5000)  # 5000 ms
        await expect(page).to_have_title("Welcome - steero practice site", timeout=3000)
        print("Title:", await page.title())

        await page.goto("products.html", wait_until="networkidle")
        await expect(page.locator("tbody tr")).to_have_count(3)
        print("Rows:", await page.locator("tbody tr").count())
        await browser.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Apart from the import, the solution only adds the course's three settings so it runs in any browser. timeout=5000 is still five seconds, because this is the compatibility layer.

docs.title: Exercise 2: the one call that cannot move
docs.text:
This ported script stops with UnsupportedFeature. Find the call, read what the error names, and replace it with something steero supports.

page.goto("http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html")
page.fill("#username", "ada")
page.fill("#password", "lovelace")
page.click("#sign-in")
expect(page.locator("#status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")
handle = page.evaluate_handle("document.getElementById('status')")
print(handle.evaluate("el => el.textContent"))
Solution 
"""Lesson 15, exercise 2: find the call that raises UnsupportedFeature, and replace it.

The ported script used ``page.evaluate_handle()`` to get a JS handle to the status line and
read its text. steero has no JS handles, so the layer raises ``UnsupportedFeature`` naming
the method. The script shows that error once, then does the same job with a locator.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os

from steero.compat.playwright import UnsupportedFeature
from steero.compat.playwright.sync_api import expect, sync_playwright

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def main() -> None:
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser_type = p.firefox if BROWSER == "firefox" else p.chromium
        channel = "msedge" if BROWSER == "edge" else None
        browser = browser_type.launch(headless=HEADLESS, channel=channel)
        page = browser.new_page()
        page.goto(BASE_URL + "login.html")
        page.fill("#username", "ada")
        page.fill("#password", "lovelace")
        page.click("#sign-in")
        expect(page.locator("#status")).to_have_text("Welcome, ada")

        try:  # the original line
            handle = page.evaluate_handle("document.getElementById('status')")
            print(handle.evaluate("el => el.textContent"))
        except UnsupportedFeature as error:
            print("Unsupported:", error.feature)

        # The replacement: a locator does what the handle did, and auto-waits as well.
        text = page.locator("#status").evaluate("el => el.textContent")
        print("Status:", text)
        assert text == "Welcome, ada"
        browser.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Unsupported: Page.evaluate_handle
Status: Welcome, ada

A JS handle is a reference to an object living in the page. A locator is a description that finds the element again, and locator.evaluate() runs the same function on it. The solution catches the error only to show its feature; in your own port, just change the line.

docs.title: Exercise 3: native, in seconds
docs.text:
Rewrite this compatibility-layer script to native steero. Convert every timeout to seconds, use steero's wait_until value, and replace the selector shortcuts with locators.

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch()
    context = browser.new_context(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
    context.set_default_timeout(10000)
    page = context.new_page()
    page.set_default_navigation_timeout(20000)
    page.goto("products.html", wait_until="load")
    page.wait_for_selector("tbody tr", timeout=2000)
    page.click("button[aria-label='Add Blue mug to cart']", timeout=500)
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("cart-count")).to_have_text("1", timeout=1500)
    browser.close()
Solution 
"""Lesson 15, exercise 3: the compatibility script from the lesson rewritten to native steero.

Every millisecond timeout became seconds (``10000`` is ``10``, ``2000`` is ``2``, ``500`` is
``0.5``), ``wait_until`` uses steero's values, and selector shortcuts became locators.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

import os

from steero.sync_api import expect, launch

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def main() -> None:
    with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS) as browser:
        context = browser.new_context(base_url=BASE_URL)
        context.set_default_timeout(10)                    # was set_default_timeout(10000)
        page = context.new_page()
        page.set_default_navigation_timeout(20)            # was set_default_navigation_timeout(20000)

        page.goto("products.html", wait_until="complete")  # was wait_until="load"
        page.locator("tbody tr").first.wait_for(timeout=2)  # was wait_for_selector("tbody tr", timeout=2000)
        add = page.get_by_role("button", name="Add Blue mug to cart")
        add.click(timeout=0.5)                             # was click(..., timeout=500)
        expect(page.get_by_test_id("cart-count")).to_have_text("1", timeout=1.5)  # was timeout=1500
        print("Cart:", page.get_by_test_id("cart-count").text_content())
        context.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Each converted line keeps the old value in a comment, which makes a migration review quick. wait_for_selector becomes locator(...).first.wait_for(): it waits for the first row to be visible, and returns nothing, because there is no handle to return.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Common mistakes

  • Moving a line to native steero and keeping its milliseconds. click(timeout=5000) in native code waits 83 minutes instead of five seconds. Convert the numbers in the same edit.
  • Mixing the layer's objects with native ones. A compat page passed to native steero.sync_api.expect raises a TypeError (currently with a confusing message such as "this assertion needs a page, not a locator"), and the reverse fails too. Import expect from the same API as the page, and move a whole script or module at a time.
  • wait_until="domcontentloaded" in native code. The browser rejects it with ProtocolError: browsingContext.navigate: invalid argument .... Native steero spells it "interactive" (and "load" is "complete").
  • page.goto(...).ok on about:blank or a data: URL. There is no network response, so goto() returns None there, in steero as in Playwright. Check for None first.
  • Expecting the plugin without -p. Without -p steero.compat.playwright.pytest (or the addopts line), pytest reports fixture 'page' not found.
  • --browser firefox is "unrecognized". pytest-playwright is installed and owns the plain options. Use --steero-browser firefox (and --steero-base-url and so on).
  • Catching UnsupportedFeature to keep a test green. The feature still does nothing. Replace the call; the error's feature tells you which one.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• from steero.compat.playwright.sync_api import ... runs Playwright code unchanged on stock Chrome, Edge and Firefox, with timeouts in milliseconds.
  • -p steero.compat.playwright.pytest keeps pytest-playwright's page and friends; it is opt-in so it never clashes with the real plugin.
  • What steero cannot do raises UnsupportedFeature naming the feature.
  • Moving to native: launch(), seconds, interactive/complete, locators, steero_page.
  • Use the layer to start quickly; write new code natively.

Next: 16. Capstone: a ControlLab suite

docs.title: 16. Capstone: a ControlLab suite
docs.text:
In this lesson

You will learn to:

  • plan a test suite for a real application: journeys, page objects and test data
  • write tests with the pytest plugin against ControlLab, using everything from the course
  • sign in once per session, use storage state, mock one request, and add a visual check
  • run the suite in Chrome and Firefox with traces kept on failure
  • build a small local gate script that runs it all and fails clearly

Time: about 90 minutes. Before this: 15. Migrating from Playwright. Code: examples/course/16-capstone/

Every lesson so far drove a small page built for that lesson. Real applications are bigger, change under you, and need a suite someone else can read and run. This lesson builds one: about ten tests against ControlLab, a single-page app with menus, a data grid, forms and dialogs, with the structure, fixtures and gate a team would keep.

docs.title: The application
docs.text:
ControlLab is a demo app that ships with steero's own test suite. The practice server serves it at /controllab/v1/, so with python examples/course/serve.py running, open http://127.0.0.1:8765/controllab/v1/index.html and sign in as admin / Admin@123 (or viewer / Viewer@123, a read-only user).

Take ten minutes to click around before writing anything:

  • Sign in (#/login): validation, a lockout after three wrong passwords, "Remember me", a "Forgot password?" dialog.
  • The shell: a menubar (Controls and Widgets open on hover, Data and Planner on click), side navigation, breadcrumbs, an account menu (Profile, Logout), toasts in the corner.
  • Data > Data Grid (#/grid): 200 employees, paging, sorting, a quick filter.
  • Widgets > Rich content: media, a chart, and images that load only when scrolled near.
  • Account: a profile form with a display name and an avatar showing its initials.

It is a hash-routed single-page app: every page is index.html#/<route>, and moving between pages changes the hash without reloading. Two details matter for testing. Its data is generated from a fixed seed, so every run sees the same 200 employees. And it keeps the signed-in session in sessionStorage, which you will meet again below.

/controllab/v2/ and /controllab/v3/ are the same app with catalogued markup changes (renamed ids, relabelled buttons, moved columns), made to test self-healing (lesson 12).

docs.title: Planning the suite
docs.text:
Start from journeys, what a user does, not from pages or functions. For ControlLab:

Journey Tests Why it matters Sign in success, wrong password, empty fields, password reset nothing else works without it Get around the menus reach a page; logout closes the app navigation breaks quietly Find data the grid shows its first page; the quick filter narrows it the app's main job Come back later "Remember me" survives in saved storage state across sessions Survive the network a mocked image response is used the app copes with what the server sends Look right the sign-in card matches its baseline layout regressions no assertion catches

Three rules keep such a suite readable:

  • One behaviour per test, named as a sentence: test_wrong_password_shows_attempts_left. The name is what you read in a failure report.
  • Assert what the user sees: the heading, the message, the URL, the row count. Not the internal state.
  • Each test starts from scratch: its own context, its own sign-in. A test that depends on the one before it fails for the wrong reason.

The folder looks like this:

examples/course/16-capstone/
    runner.py            builds the pytest command line, runs it in-process
    example_run_suite.py the worked example: record the baseline, run the suite
    suite/
        pytest.ini       markers and options; makes this folder pytest's rootdir
        conftest.py      fixtures
        pages.py         two page objects
        test_login.py  test_navigation.py  test_grid.py
        test_storage.py  test_network.py  test_visual.py
        exercises/       tests for the exercises (not collected by default)

docs.title: Page objects, lightly
docs.text:
A page object is a class that names the locators of one screen and the few actions a user takes there. It saves repeating page.get_by_label("Password", exact=True) in ten tests, and when the form changes, one file changes.

"""Lesson 16: two light page objects for ControlLab, the sign-in page and the app shell.

A page object here only names locators and a few actions a user takes. Assertions stay in the
tests, so a failing test still reads as a list of what the user saw.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from steero.sync_api import Healer, Locator, Page, expect


class LoginPage:
    """The sign-in form at ``#/login``.

    Args:
        page: The page to drive.
        healer: When given, the submit button heals under the key ``login.submit`` if its
            markup changes (lesson 12).
    """

    def __init__(self, page: Page, healer: Healer | None = None):
        self.page = page
        self.username = page.get_by_label("Username")
        self.password = page.get_by_label("Password", exact=True)  # not the "Show password" button
        self.remember = page.get_by_label("Remember me")
        submit = page.get_by_role("button", name="Login", exact=True)
        self.submit = healer.locator("login.submit", submit) if healer else submit
        self.error = page.get_by_test_id("login-error")

    def open(self) -> None:
        """Load the app at the sign-in route."""
        self.page.goto("index.html#/login")
        expect(self.username).to_be_visible()

    def sign_in(self, user: str, password: str, *, remember: bool = False) -> None:
        """Fill in the form and submit it."""
        self.username.fill(user)
        self.password.fill(password)
        if remember:
            self.remember.check()
        self.submit.click()


class Shell:
    """Everything around a signed-in page: heading, menus, account menu, toasts."""

    def __init__(self, page: Page):
        self.page = page
        self.heading = page.get_by_role("heading", level=1)
        self.account_menu = page.get_by_role("button", name="Account menu")

    def navigate(self, menu: str, item: str) -> None:
        """Open a top-level menu and choose an item, as a user would."""
        self.page.get_by_role("menubar").get_by_role("menuitem", name=menu, exact=True).click()
        self.page.get_by_role("menu", name=menu).get_by_role("menuitem", name=item, exact=True).click()

    def logout(self) -> None:
        """Log out through the account menu."""
        self.account_menu.click()
        self.page.get_by_role("menuitem", name="Logout").click()

    def toast(self, text: str) -> Locator:
        """The notification that contains ``text``."""
        return self.page.get_by_test_id("toast").filter(has_text=text)

Keep them light. These hold locators and actions, but no assertions: a test that reads login.sign_in("admin", "nope") then expect(login.error).to_have_text(...) still tells you what was checked. A page object that grows methods like verify_login_failed() hides the check, and a suite of them reads like a list of function names. Make one only for screens that several tests use; a one-off page is clearer inline.

Two details in LoginPage. get_by_label("Password", exact=True) matters because the "Show password" button's label also contains "password". And the submit button goes through a healer when the test has one, under the stable key login.submit (lesson 12), which pays off in exercise 3.

Coming from Selenium

Selenium page objects often wrap every element in a method and wait explicitly in each one. Here a locator is the element description, and every action and expect waits by itself, so a page object is mostly a list of attributes.

docs.title: Fixtures for the suite
docs.text:
The suite uses steero's pytest plugin (lesson 09): steero_page gives each test a fresh page in its own context, steero_browser is one browser for the session, and the plugin reads --steero-base-url, so page.goto("index.html#/login") resolves against the ControlLab folder. conftest.py builds the suite's own fixtures on top:

"""Lesson 16: fixtures for the ControlLab suite, built on steero's pytest plugin.

* ``page``: steero's ``steero_page`` with a desktop viewport. Relative URLs resolve against
  ``--steero-base-url`` (the ControlLab folder, ending in ``/``).
* ``login``: the sign-in page object, its submit button guarded by ``steero_healer``.
* ``admin_session``: signs in once per session and keeps the session ControlLab stored.
* ``signed_in``: a page that starts signed in, by giving the new context that session.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re

import pytest
from pages import LoginPage, Shell

from steero.heal import FingerprintStore
from steero.sync_api import Browser, BrowserContext, Healer, Page, expect, healer

ADMIN = ("admin", "Admin@123")


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def app_url(pytestconfig: pytest.Config) -> str:
    """The ControlLab folder the suite runs against, from ``--steero-base-url``."""
    url = pytestconfig.getoption("steero_base_url")
    if not url:
        raise pytest.UsageError("pass --steero-base-url http://127.0.0.1:8765/controllab/v1/")
    return str(url)


@pytest.fixture
def page(steero_page: Page) -> Page:
    """A fresh page in its own context, sized like a laptop screen."""
    steero_page.set_viewport_size({"width": 1366, "height": 900})
    return steero_page


@pytest.fixture
def login(page: Page, steero_healer: Healer) -> LoginPage:
    """The sign-in page, already open."""
    login_page = LoginPage(page, steero_healer)
    login_page.open()
    return login_page


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def admin_session(steero_browser: Browser, steero_store: FingerprintStore, app_url: str) -> str:
    """Sign in through the form once, and return the session ControlLab saved.

    ControlLab keeps its session in ``sessionStorage``, which ``storage_state`` does not
    capture, so the value is read directly and handed to each test's context below.
    """
    context = steero_browser.new_context(base_url=app_url)
    try:
        page = context.new_page()
        form = LoginPage(page, healer(page, steero_store))
        form.open()
        form.sign_in(*ADMIN)
        expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"#/home$"))
        session = page.evaluate("sessionStorage.getItem('cl.session')")
    finally:
        context.close()
    assert session, "signing in stored no session"
    return str(session)


@pytest.fixture
def signed_in(page: Page, steero_context: BrowserContext, admin_session: str) -> Shell:
    """A page on Home, signed in as admin without going through the form again."""
    steero_context.add_init_script(
        "try { if (!sessionStorage.getItem('cl.session'))"
        f" sessionStorage.setItem('cl.session', {json.dumps(admin_session)}); }} catch (e) {{}}")
    page.goto("index.html#/home")
    shell = Shell(page)
    expect(shell.heading).to_have_text("Home")
    return shell
  • page is steero_page with a laptop-sized viewport, so the menubar is shown (narrow windows get a drawer instead).
  • login opens the sign-in page and hands back the page object.
  • admin_session is session-scoped: it signs in through the form once for the whole run and keeps what ControlLab stored.
  • signed_in gives a test's context that session before the page loads, and lands on Home. Ten tests that need a signed-in user do not each type a password.

Why not storage_state here? context.storage_state() saves cookies and localStorage, the way Playwright does. ControlLab keeps its session in sessionStorage, which belongs to one tab and is not part of storage state. So the fixture reads the value once and writes it back with context.add_init_script(), which runs before the app's own scripts on every page of the context. Check where your own application keeps its session before choosing: for a cookie or localStorage session, new_context(storage_state="state.json") is all you need, and test_storage.py shows it with ControlLab's "Remember me", which does live in localStorage.

The sign-in tests use the page object and assert what appears:

"""Lesson 16: the sign-in journey, through the form a user sees.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from pages import LoginPage, Shell

from steero.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_admin_signs_in_and_lands_on_home(page: Page, login: LoginPage) -> None:
    login.sign_in("admin", "Admin@123")
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"#/home$"))
    expect(Shell(page).heading).to_have_text("Home")
    expect(page.get_by_text("Welcome back")).to_contain_text("Alex Admin")


def test_wrong_password_shows_attempts_left(page: Page, login: LoginPage) -> None:
    login.sign_in("admin", "nope")
    expect(login.error).to_have_text("Invalid username or password (2 attempts left)")
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"#/login$"))


def test_empty_fields_show_inline_errors(page: Page, login: LoginPage) -> None:
    login.submit.click()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Username is required")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Password is required")).to_be_visible()


def test_forgot_password_sends_a_reset_link(page: Page, login: LoginPage) -> None:
    page.get_by_role("link", name="Forgot password?").click()
    dialog = page.get_by_role("dialog", name="Reset your password")
    dialog.get_by_label("Email address").fill("not-an-email")
    dialog.get_by_role("button", name="Send link").click()
    expect(dialog.get_by_text("Enter a valid email address")).to_be_visible()

    dialog.get_by_label("Email address").fill("ada@example.com")
    dialog.get_by_role("button", name="Send link").click()
    expect(dialog).to_be_hidden()
    expect(Shell(page).toast("Reset link sent to ada@example.com")).to_be_visible()

The password reset test is the suite's form: it fills the dialog wrong, checks the inline error, fills it right, and checks that the dialog closed and a toast confirmed it. Scoping the locators to page.get_by_role("dialog", name="Reset your password") keeps them from matching anything behind the dialog.

The grid tests read a column by its header, not by a fixed position. ControlLab v2 moves the Department column, and a test that counted columns would then read the wrong one:

"""Lesson 16: the data grid, its paging status and the quick filter.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from pages import Shell

from steero.sync_api import Locator, Page, expect


def department_cells(page: Page) -> Locator:
    """The Department cell of every row on the current grid page, found by its column header."""
    grid = page.get_by_role("grid", name="Employees")
    headers = [text.strip() for text in grid.get_by_role("columnheader").all_inner_texts()]
    column = headers.index("Department") + 1  # read the position each time: columns can move
    return grid.locator(f"tbody tr td:nth-child({column})")


@pytest.fixture
def grid(signed_in: Shell) -> Page:
    """The Data Grid page, reached through the menus."""
    signed_in.navigate("Data", "Data Grid")
    expect(signed_in.page.get_by_test_id("grid-status")).to_contain_text("Showing")
    return signed_in.page


def test_grid_shows_the_first_page_of_200_employees(grid: Page) -> None:
    expect(grid.get_by_test_id("grid-status")).to_have_text("Showing 1 to 25 of 200")
    expect(department_cells(grid)).to_have_count(25)


def test_quick_filter_narrows_to_one_department(grid: Page) -> None:
    grid.get_by_label("Quick filter").fill("Engineering")

Storage state, with a second context made from the saved file:

"""Lesson 16: "Remember me" survives in a saved storage state.

ControlLab stores the remembered user name in ``localStorage``, which ``storage_state``
captures. A new context started from that state opens the form with the name filled in.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

from pages import LoginPage

from steero.sync_api import Browser, BrowserContext, Page, expect


def test_remember_me_survives_in_storage_state(page: Page, login: LoginPage, steero_context: BrowserContext,
                                               steero_browser: Browser, app_url: str, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    login.sign_in("viewer", "Viewer@123", remember=True)
    expect(page).to_have_url(re.compile(r"#/home$"))
    state = tmp_path / "state.json"
    steero_context.storage_state(path=state)

    later = steero_browser.new_context(storage_state=str(state), base_url=app_url)

        later.close()

One mocked request. ControlLab has no server API: everything it loads is a file. Its lazy-loaded images are the requests whose result a user can see, so the test answers the first one itself, with a small SVG, and checks that the page used it (the real picture is 320 pixels wide, the mock 64):

"""Lesson 16: one mocked request. The first lazy-loaded image is answered by the test itself.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
Modified: Nov-07-2026 (sync route handlers get a sync Route now)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from pages import Shell

from steero.sync_api import expect

PICTURE = ('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="64" height="36">'
           '<rect width="64" height="36" fill="teal"/></svg>')


def test_a_mocked_image_counts_as_loaded(signed_in: Shell) -> None:
    page = signed_in.page
    # One call, so a lambda; a handler with several steps would be an ordinary def.
    page.route("**/assets/lazy-1.svg", lambda route: route.fulfill(body=PICTURE, content_type="image/svg+xml"))
    signed_in.navigate("Widgets", "Rich content")
    for image in page.get_by_role("img", name=re.compile(r"^Lazy image")).all():
        image.scroll_into_view_if_needed()  # they load only near the viewport, 400 px apart

    expect(page.get_by_test_id("lazy-status")).to_have_text("Loaded 3 of 3")
    width = page.get_by_role("img", name="Lazy image A").evaluate("img => img.naturalWidth")
    assert width == 64, f"the page shows the real picture, not the mock (width {width})"

One visual check, of the sign-in card only (the Home page shows the time of day, which would never match). It is marked visual, so it can be run, or left out, on its own:

"""Lesson 16: one visual check, the sign-in card against its recorded baseline.

Baselines are per browser and platform (``login-card-chrome-win32.png``); where they live is
set by ``STEERO_SNAPSHOT_DIR``. Record them with ``STEERO_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1``.

"""

import pytest
from pages import LoginPage

from steero.sync_api import Page, expect

def test_login_card_looks_unchanged(page: Page, login: LoginPage) -> None:

Baselines are per browser and platform (login-card-chrome-win32.png), as lesson 05 explained. In a project you commit them; the course scripts record them in a temporary folder first, through STEERO_SNAPSHOT_DIR and STEERO_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1, so they never write into the repository.

Browser support

Every test runs in Chrome (both backends), Edge and Firefox without a browser check. The one browser difference that showed up while writing them was lazy loading: Firefox loads a lazy image only when it is close to the viewport, so the network test scrolls each image into view rather than just the section heading.

docs.title: Running it well
docs.text:
runner.py builds the command line in one place, so every script runs the suite the same way:

"""Lesson 16: build the pytest command line for the capstone suite, and run it in this process.

Imported by the lesson's scripts; not an example on its own. Every output (per-test traces,
failure artifacts, heal baselines and reports, screenshot baselines) goes under one folder
the caller chooses, never into the repository.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

SUITE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "suite"


def suite_args(output: Path, *, browsers: Sequence[str], base_url: str, version: str = "v1",
               targets: Sequence[str] = (), extra: Sequence[str] = (), headed: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """The pytest arguments for one run of the suite.

    Args:
        output: Folder for everything the run writes.
        browsers: Browsers to run every test in (``chrome``, ``firefox``, ``edge``).
        base_url: The practice site's address, ending in ``/``.
        version: ControlLab version to test: ``v1``, ``v2`` or ``v3``.
        targets: Test files or node ids; the whole suite when empty.
        extra: More pytest arguments, such as ``-m visual`` or ``--steero-strict-heal``.
        headed: Show the browser windows.
    """
    args = [*(targets or [str(SUITE)]), "-q",
            "--steero-base-url", f"{base_url}controllab/{version}/",
            "--steero-output", str(output / "test-results"),
            "--steero-tracing", "retain-on-failure",
            "--steero-artifacts", str(output / "steero-artifacts"),
            "--steero-baselines", str(output / "heal-baselines")]
    for browser in browsers:
        args += ["--steero-browser", browser]
    if headed:
        args.append("--steero-headed")
    return [*args, *extra]


def run(args: Sequence[str], *, snapshots: Path, update_snapshots: bool = False) -> int:
    """Run pytest in this process with screenshot baselines in ``snapshots``; return its exit code."""
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True  # keep __pycache__ out of the examples folder
    os.environ["STEERO_SNAPSHOT_DIR"] = str(snapshots)
    if update_snapshots:
        os.environ["STEERO_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS"] = "1"
    try:
        return int(pytest.main(list(args)))
    finally:
        os.environ.pop("STEERO_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS", None)


def traces(output: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """The traces kept for failed tests (``--steero-tracing retain-on-failure``)."""
    return sorted((output / "test-results").glob("*/trace.zip"))

The options worth knowing:

Option Effect --steero-browser chrome --steero-browser firefox every test runs once per browser (the test id ends in [chrome] or [firefox]) --steero-base-url URL relative goto() URLs resolve against it --steero-tracing retain-on-failure record a trace of every test, keep it only for failures (steero show-trace, lesson 10) --steero-output DIR per-test folders for traces, screenshots and video --steero-artifacts DIR failure screenshot, HTML and console output; the heal report --steero-baselines DIR the self-healing fingerprints --steero-strict-heal a test that needed healing fails, so a heal is fixed rather than forgotten -m visual, -m "not visual" only, or all but, the visual check

The --steero- spellings always work; the plain --browser, --tracing and so on also work when pytest-playwright is not installed (lesson 15). From a terminal, the same run is:

pytest examples/course/16-capstone/suite --steero-browser firefox --steero-base-url http://127.0.0.1:8765/controllab/v1/ --steero-tracing retain-on-failure

docs.text:
example_run_suite.py runs the suite in the course browser, in two pytest runs: first it records the visual baseline, then it runs everything and exits non-zero if any test failed.

"""Lesson 16: run the capstone suite against ControlLab v1 in the course browser.

Two pytest runs, as a real project does them. First the visual baseline is recorded (a
project commits it; here it goes to a temporary folder), then the whole suite runs with
traces kept for any test that fails. The script exits non-zero if any test failed.

    python examples/course/16-capstone/example_run_suite.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

# course: timeout=240

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from runner import run, suite_args, traces

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def main() -> None:
    output = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="capstone-"))
    snapshots = output / "snapshots"
    common = {"browsers": [BROWSER], "base_url": BASE_URL, "headed": not HEADLESS}

    print("1. Recording the visual baseline")
    code = run(suite_args(output, **common, extra=["-m", "visual"]), snapshots=snapshots, update_snapshots=True)
    assert code == 0, f"recording the baseline failed (exit {code})"

    print("2. Running the suite")
    code = run(suite_args(output, **common), snapshots=snapshots)
    for trace in traces(output):
        print("trace kept:", trace)
    print(f"Suite exited {code}; outputs in {output}")
    if code != 0:
        raise SystemExit(code)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Exercise 1: a new display name everywhere
docs.text:
Write a test that opens Account (account menu > Profile), changes the display name from "Alex Admin" to "Ada Lovelace", saves, and checks it everywhere it shows: the field, the avatar's initials, the "Profile saved" toast, the Home page's recent activity, and the field again after coming back.

Solution 
"""Lesson 16, exercise 1: change the display name and check it everywhere it appears.

The name shows in the Display name field, as initials in the avatar preview, in a toast when
saved, in the Home page's recent activity, and it must still be there after leaving the page.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pages import Shell

from steero.sync_api import expect


def open_profile(shell: Shell) -> None:
    """Account menu > Profile."""
    shell.account_menu.click()
    shell.page.get_by_role("menuitem", name="Profile").click()
    expect(shell.heading).to_have_text("Account")


def test_display_name_change_shows_everywhere(signed_in: Shell) -> None:
    page = signed_in.page
    name = page.get_by_label("Display name")
    avatar = page.get_by_test_id("avatar-preview")

    open_profile(signed_in)
    expect(name).to_have_value("Alex Admin")
    expect(avatar).to_have_text("AA")

    name.fill("Ada Lovelace")
    expect(avatar).to_have_text("AL")  # the initials follow as you type
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Save profile").click()
    expect(signed_in.toast("Profile saved")).to_be_visible()

    page.get_by_role("menubar").get_by_role("menuitem", name="Home").click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("region", name="Recent activity")).to_contain_text("Updated account profile")

    open_profile(signed_in)  # leave and come back: the change was saved, not just typed
    expect(name).to_have_value("Ada Lovelace")
    expect(avatar).to_have_text("AL")

docs.title: Exercise 3: ControlLab v2, healed
docs.text:
Run the suite against v1 to record fingerprints, then against v2 with the same --steero-baselines, and read heal-report.json. Which locator healed, what did steero suggest instead, and how sure was it?

Solution 
"""Lesson 16, exercise 3: run the suite against ControlLab v2 with healing, and read the heal report.

ControlLab v2 renames the Login button to "Sign in" and changes its id. Run 1 (v1) records
the button's fingerprint under the key ``login.submit``; run 2 (v2) uses the same baselines,
so the healer finds the renamed button and reports what it did. The visual test is left out:
on v2 the card really does look different, and a visual check should say so.

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

# course: timeout=300

import json
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from runner import run, suite_args

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def main() -> None:
    output = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="capstone-heal-"))
    common = {"browsers": [BROWSER], "base_url": BASE_URL, "headed": not HEADLESS, "extra": ["-m", "not visual"]}

    print("1. v1: recording fingerprints")
    assert run(suite_args(output, version="v1", **common), snapshots=output / "snapshots") == 0

    print("2. v2: the same tests, healing where the markup changed")
    code = run(suite_args(output, version="v2", **common), snapshots=output / "snapshots")

    report = output / "steero-artifacts" / "heal-report.json"
    events = json.loads(report.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if report.is_file() else []
    for event in events:
        print(f"{event['outcome']:8} {event['key']}: {event['locator']} -> {event['suggestion']} "
              f"({event['score']:.2f}) in {event['test']}")
    assert code == 0, f"the v2 run failed (exit {code})"
    assert any(e["key"] == "login.submit" and e["outcome"] == "healed" for e in events), "nothing healed"
    print(f"Report: {report}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

HEALED  login.submit [warn 0.75] get_by_role('button', name='Login') -> page.get_by_test_id('login-submit')
...
healed   login.submit: get_by_role('button', name='Login') -> page.get_by_test_id('login-submit') (0.75) in test_login.py::test_admin_signs_in_and_lands_on_home[chrome]

v2 renames the button to "Sign in", so the role-and-name locator finds nothing; the healer scores every candidate against the fingerprint from v1 and picks the submit button with 0.75, in the warn band (lesson 12), which also raises a SelfHealWarning. Everything else passes on v2 unchanged, because the other locators already describe what the user sees (labels, roles, headers) rather than ids. The fix is the suggestion: update the page object, and the next run needs no healing. The visual test is left out with -m "not visual": on v2 the card does look different, and that check should fail.

docs.title: Exercise 4: a gate
docs.text:
Write one script a developer runs before pushing: it runs the whole suite in every installed browser (skipping any that is missing), records the visual baselines first, uses --steero-strict-heal, keeps traces on failure, exits non-zero on any failure, and prints where the traces are.

Solution 
"""Lesson 16, exercise 4: a local gate that runs the whole suite in every installed browser.

One command a developer runs before pushing. It records the visual baselines, runs every
test in Chrome and Firefox (whichever are installed) with ``--steero-strict-heal``, so a test
that only passed thanks to healing fails the gate, and keeps a trace for every failure. It
exits non-zero on any failure and prints where the traces are.

    python examples/course/16-capstone/solution_4_gate.py

Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy
Date: Nov-07-2026
"""

# course: browsers=chrome
# course: timeout=400

import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from runner import run, suite_args, traces

from steero import LaunchError
from steero.launch.discover import find_browser

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"


def installed(names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """The browsers from ``names`` that steero can find on this machine."""
    found = []
    for name in names:
        try:
            find_browser(name)
        except LaunchError:
            print(f"gate: {name} is not installed, skipped")
        else:
            found.append(name)
    return found


def main() -> None:
    browsers = installed(["chrome", "firefox"])
    if not browsers:
        raise SystemExit("gate: no browser to run in")
    output = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="capstone-gate-"))
    snapshots = output / "snapshots"
    common = {"browsers": browsers, "base_url": BASE_URL, "headed": not HEADLESS}

    steps = [("visual baselines", suite_args(output, **common, extra=["-m", "visual"]), True),
             ("suite", suite_args(output, **common, extra=["--steero-strict-heal"]), False)]
    for title, args, update in steps:
        print(f"gate: {title} in {', '.join(browsers)}")
        code = run(args, snapshots=snapshots, update_snapshots=update)
        if code != 0:
            print(f"gate: FAILED at {title} (pytest exit {code})")
            for trace in traces(output):
                print(f"  trace: {trace}   open it with: steero show-trace \"{trace}\"")
            print(f"  failure artifacts: {output / 'steero-artifacts'}")
            raise SystemExit(1)
    print(f"gate: passed in {', '.join(browsers)}; outputs in {output}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

gate: visual baselines in chrome, firefox
2 passed, 20 deselected in 13.99s
gate: suite in chrome, firefox
22 passed in 51.75s
gate: passed in chrome, firefox; outputs in C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Temp\capstone-gate-fqa6g_yt

--steero-strict-heal turns a heal into a failure: healing keeps a suite running while you find out what changed, but a gate should not let a changed locator through unnoticed. steero has no CI setup of its own; a gate script like this is what a CI job would call.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
Common mistakes

  • Tests that depend on each other. The second test passes only after the first signed in. Each test gets its own context; build what it needs with fixtures, never with test order.
  • Expecting storage_state to keep a sessionStorage session. It saves cookies and localStorage only, so the "signed-in" context lands on the sign-in page. Find where the app keeps its session; seed sessionStorage with add_init_script, as conftest.py does.
  • An async def route handler in this sync suite. It is given the async Route and must await route.fulfill(...); a forgotten await leaves the request to the real server (RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'Route.fulfill' was never awaited). In sync code write the handler as a lambda or an ordinary def: it gets a sync Route and runs on a worker thread, so it can make as many calls as it needs.
  • Reading grid cells by a fixed column number. It breaks the day a column moves. Find the column from its header, as test_grid.py does.
  • A visual check of a page with the time on it. It never matches. Check a stable element, or mask= the moving parts.
  • no baseline existed; wrote ... on the first run. That is deliberate: a missing baseline never passes silently. Look at the file, then run again (or record with STEERO_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1).
  • Leaving outputs in the repository. Point --steero-output, --steero-artifacts, --steero-baselines and STEERO_SNAPSHOT_DIR at a folder you mean (the scripts use a temporary one), and keep -p no:cacheprovider or ignore .pytest_cache.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• Plan by journeys; one behaviour per test, named as a sentence, asserting what the user sees.
  • Keep page objects light: locators and actions, assertions in the tests.
  • Session-scoped fixtures do expensive setup once; each test still gets a fresh context.
  • --steero-browser twice, --steero-tracing retain-on-failure and --steero-strict-heal make a suite that runs everywhere, explains its failures and does not hide changes.
  • A small gate script that exits non-zero is the whole release check.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
You have finished the course. From here:

  • The guides are the reference for everything the lessons touched, with every option listed: locators, auto-waiting, network, emulation, tracing, self-healing, the pytest plugin, MCP.
  • The API reference lists every class and method.
  • ControlLab's own suite, tests/integration/controllab/ in the repository, is the full version of this capstone: about 280 tests over 13 journeys, with a locator registry, brittle and resilient styles, and measurements of healing on v2 and v3. Read a journey or two to see the same ideas at scale.
  • Contribute. When you find a browser behaving differently from the WebDriver BiDi specification, steero records it in Upstream findings, with the command and the browser version; a clear finding helps the browser teams fix it. Bug reports and small fixes to steero are welcome too, as are corrections to this course.

Back to the course home.

docs.title: Course conventions
docs.text: How the lessons are written and how their code is laid out. Learners can skim this page to know what the boxes mean; lesson writers should follow it closely, so that sixteen lessons read like one course. Lesson 01 is the reference: when in doubt, copy what it does.

docs.title: The boxes
docs.text: Box Markdown Use it for In this lesson !!! abstract "In this lesson" The opening box: objectives, time, prerequisites, example folder. Once per lesson, first. Coming from Playwright !!! tip "Coming from Playwright" What a Playwright user would do differently or expect wrongly. Put it next to the concept it is about, not in a pile at the end. Coming from Selenium !!! tip "Coming from Selenium" The same for Selenium habits (explicit waits, find_element, driver binaries). Browser support !!! note "Browser support" Any difference between Chrome and Firefox (or Edge): an option that is Chrome only, a different mechanism, a known gap. Common mistakes !!! warning "Common mistakes" Once per lesson, after the exercises: the errors learners actually hit, each with its symptom and fix. Solution ??? success "Solution" Collapsed solution under every exercise. The ??? makes it start closed. Async version ??? example "Async version" The async form of a sync snippet, where the difference matters.

docs.title: Lesson page template
docs.text:
Each lesson is docs/course/NN-slug.md. Keep this order:

# NN. Title

<!-- Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy | Date: Nov-07-2026 -->

!!! abstract "In this lesson"
    **You will learn to:** three to six objectives, each a verb you can check.

    **Time:** about N minutes. **Before this:** [lesson NN-1](...). **Code:** `examples/course/NN-slug/`

One or two sentences on why this matters, in the learner's terms.

## A concept section per idea
Short prose, then a small snippet. Link the guide for the full reference.

## Worked example
What the script does, then the script itself, included from the examples folder:

```python
--8<-- "examples/course/NN-slug/example_topic.py"
```

How to run it, and what it prints.

## Exercises
### Exercise 1: short title
The task, a hint if it helps, and how the learner knows they got it right.

??? success "Solution"
    ```python
    --8<-- "examples/course/NN-slug/solution_1_topic.py"
    ```

    A line on why the solution works, or the trap it avoids.

## Common mistakes
!!! warning "Common mistakes"
    - **Symptom.** Cause and fix.

## Recap
Three to five bullets.

**Next:** [NN+1. Title](NN+1-slug.md)

Writers: replace the <!-- STATUS: stub ... --> line with <!-- STATUS: written, owner: <name> --> when the lesson is done, and keep the stub's section plan unless the code shows a better one.

docs.title: Code in lessons
docs.text:
• Sync API first. Learners start with from steero.sync_api import expect, launch. Show async where it changes something: event handlers, running things concurrently, or the first time a lesson's API appears (in an ??? example "Async version" box). The pytest lessons are sync throughout.
  • Seconds for every timeout. click(timeout=2) is two seconds. Say "seconds" in the prose the first time a lesson sets one. Milliseconds appear only in lesson 15, for the Playwright compatibility layer, and are labelled there.
  • Runnable code is included, never pasted. A worked example or solution in a lesson comes from its file with a snippet line (--8<-- "examples/course/..."), so the page shows exactly what the course test runs. Short illustrative fragments (three to ten lines) may be inline.
  • Only real APIs. Every name used must exist in steero today. Check the code or the API reference; do not write what Playwright would accept.
  • Prefer user-facing locators (get_by_role, get_by_label, get_by_text) and web-first assertions (expect(...)). No time.sleep() or wait_for_timeout() in examples, except in lesson 03 to show why not.

docs.title: Example files
docs.text:
Each lesson has a folder examples/course/NN-slug/ with a README.md (what each file shows and how to run it) and its scripts:

File Purpose Run by the course test example_<topic>.py A worked example from the lesson yes solution_<N>_<topic>.py The solution to exercise N yes anything else (test_*.py, conftest.py, data files) Material an example uses, such as a small test suite that example_run_tests.py runs with pytest no

Every runnable script:

  1. starts with a module docstring: the lesson, what it shows, how to run it, then Author: Pandiyaraj Karuppasamy and Date: <Mon-DD-YYYY>;

  2. reads its settings from the environment with these three lines, unchanged:

    BASE_URL = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/")
BROWSER = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER", "chrome")
HEADLESS = os.environ.get("STEERO_COURSE_HEADED") != "1"

  3. builds page URLs as BASE_URL + "login.html" and launches with launch(BROWSER, headless=HEADLESS);

  4. has a typed main() -> None (or async def main() -> None) and an if __name__ == "__main__": guard;
  5. prints a line or two saying what happened, and lets a failure raise, so the exit code is non-zero. Do not catch an error just to print it, unless showing the error is the lesson;
  6. writes any files (screenshots, traces, downloads) to relative paths: the course test runs each script in a fresh temporary folder;
  7. stays short: one idea per example, about 60 lines at most.

Two optional directive comments, each on a line of its own, tune the course test:

  • # course: browsers=chrome runs the script only on the listed browsers (comma separated), for Chrome-only features. Say so in a Browser support box in the lesson too.
  • # course: timeout=180 raises the per-script limit from 90 seconds.

Examples must pass ruff check. They are not type-checked by mypy (the folders are not Python packages and file names repeat between lessons, which mypy cannot handle), but write them with type hints anyway: the course test runs every one of them, which checks more than mypy would.

docs.title: The practice site
docs.text:
examples/course/serve.py serves the practice site on http://127.0.0.1:8765/:

Path Contents / Course pages, examples/course/site/ /testsite/ steero's integration-test pages, tests/site/ (forms, frames, shadow DOM, drag and drop): reuse them, never edit them for the course /controllab/v1/ (and v2/, v3/) The ControlLab app /api/... Dynamic endpoints: products JSON, echo, slow responses, status codes, a CSV download, basic auth. The full list is on the site's home page and in ENDPOINTS in serve.py

A lesson that needs its own page adds examples/course/site/<topic>.html (named after the topic, not the lesson number), using course.css and the same header, and adds one line to the "Course pages" list in site/index.html. A lesson that needs a new endpoint adds it to serve.py and to both endpoint lists. Keep pages small and deterministic: no randomness, no external requests, delays of a second or less.

docs.title: Prose
docs.text:
• Plain, precise and encouraging. Second person ("you"), present tense, short sentences. No marketing words.
  • No em dashes or en dashes, anywhere: use a comma, a colon, parentheses or two sentences.
  • Introduce a term once, in bold, then use it the same way every time.

  • Show commands for both shells where they differ (setting an environment variable):

    $env:STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER = "firefox"

    export STEERO_COURSE_BROWSER=firefox

  • Link to the guides for the full reference instead of repeating them: the course teaches, the guides list.
